subject.title: refactor(macos): move PortGuardian state to SQLite

question: Should OpenClaw accept the intentional one-way macOS PortGuardian cutover, where downgraded JSON-only copies cannot share migrated tunnel-receipt state?
rationale: The implementation deliberately trades downgrade interoperability for a single canonical durable store and fail-closed mixed-version behavior; that upgrade policy cannot be inferred safely from code correctness alone.

options.title: Accept the one-way cutover after proof
options.body: Approve SQLite-only runtime ownership once the cleanup defect is fixed, the prerequisite stack lands, and final-head signed migration and recovery evidence is attached.

options.title: Require downgrade compatibility
options.body: Keep or design a supported migration/rollback path if maintainers consider older macOS app copies a required coexistence contract.

options.title: Defer the migration
options.body: Pause this PR until macOS storage-version and downgrade policy are decided independently of the implementation stack.

recommendation.title: Accept the one-way cutover after proof
recommendation.body: Approve SQLite-only runtime ownership once the cleanup defect is fixed, the prerequisite stack lands, and final-head signed migration and recovery evidence is attached.

likelyOwner.reason: The contributor owns the active stacked native-state design and has explicitly surfaced this policy decision in the PR description.
